players.note: Derwin James was excellent in Week 1, racking up seven solos, three assists, and one pass defended. Derwin remains a DB1 play for the 2026 season and will climb into the top-five discussion given the right matchup. He will have just that in Week 2 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Start Derwin everywhere.

Nick Cross was excellent in his Commanders debut, reeling off five solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss. Cross is in the weekly DB1 conversation but becomes a top-10 play when he has plus matchups, as he does this week against the Dallas Cowboys. Start Cross everywhere.

Quentin Lake went off in Week 1, exploding with seven solos, three assists, one interception, and three passes defended. Treat Quentin as a DB1 option for Week 2's plus matchup against the New York Giants. Needless to say, Lake should be started in every and all formats.

Jordan Battle was excellent in Week 1, tallying six solos and three assists. He played every snap, and with Dax Hill now playing on the outside, Battle is expected to dominate the safety snaps at the line of scrimmage for the safety group, raising his weekly floor. Tap Battle as a top-10 option for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Houston Texans,

Dillon Thieneman showed out in Week 1, flashing with eight solos, two assists, and one pass defended against the Carolina Panthers. Thieneman played every snap in Week 1 and will continue to get all the work he can handle for the Chicago Bears, even when Coby Bryant and Xavier Woods are healthy. He flashed his DB1 upside in Week 1, but should settle in as more of a DB3 who could push for the DB2 conversation during the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Caleb Downs showed up in his NFL debut, recording four solos, four assists, and one forced fumble. Downs spent 54 of his 61 snaps playing nickel (34 snaps) or deep (20 snaps), with just seven of his snaps coming in the box. Still, the box package is an encouraging development that could help raise his weekly floor. For now, keep him in the DB3 realm for Week 2, while monitoring his snap alignment.

Julian Love was excellent in Week 1, reeling off four solos, two assists, two tackles for loss, one interception, and one pass defended. Love is locked in the DB1 conversation, albeit on the lower end of the spectrum, when he has plus matchups, and is an excellent DB2 play all other weeks. Love is a DB2 option for Week 2, thanks to a plus matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Start him where possible.

Jaquan Brisker was excellent in Week 1, reeling off four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended for the Steelers. Brisker played every snap alongside former All-Pro duo Jalen Ramsey. Jaquan is expected to have a heavy box role, as evidenced by the 57 percent of the time he lined up there in Week 1, putting him in the DB2 mix going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 2 matchup against the New England Patriots.

Kevin Winston showed up in Week 1, notching four solos and six assists. Winston is a DB2 option who is pushing to be part of the DB1 discussion. Count him as a top-20 play for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Amani Hooker impressed in Week 1, racking up six solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Hooker plays near the line of scrimmage while Kevin Byard patrols deep, so Hooker has weekly DB3 upside. Treat him as such for what should be a busy afternoon against the Philadelphia Eagles.

CJGJ played every snap in Week 1, responding with six solos and two assists for the Buffalo Bills. The mercurial safety has always been an IDP asset when he has been healthy and on an active NFL roster, and he looks poised to push his way back into the DB1 conversation. For now, tap him as a DB2 play for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Evan Williams showed up in Week 1, tallying six solos and one assist. Williams has DB2 upside but will remain more of a DB3 play until he shows more consistency. Treat him as such for a tasty Week 2 matchup against the New York Jets.
Cam Bynum showed up in Week 1, racking up seven solos. Bynum is a solid DB3 with DB2 upside and should be counted as one for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Jonas Sanker impressed in Week 1, reeling off seven solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Sanker played 66 percent of the snaps in Week 1, coming off the field when the Saints didn't need a nickel/slot back. Sanker's upside will be capped if he stays under the 70 percent snap share mark for the entire season, but playing the STAR role will provide him with some high levearage opportunities. Sanker is a solid depth piece who you can start during the byes, but you don't want to be starting him in Week 2, unless you play in a 20+ team league. Keep Sanker stashed but look elsewhere for Week 2.

Dax Hill impressed in Week 1, racking up seven solos. Hill has moved to outside corner full time, so he makes for an excellent CB1 candidate, but his weekly upside is likely capped. He will be one of the better tackling outside corners, so he should still have bye week value, but this will likely serve as a high watermark from solo tackle and possibly even total tackle perspective. Tap Hill as a CB1 but take another week before plugging him into lineups in DB leagues.

Marlon Humphrey was excellent in Week 1, reeling off three solos, one assist, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. Humphrey has managed to stay in the DB2 conversation as a corner, and outings like this highlight why. Tap Humphrey as a DB3 option for Week 2 where needed.

Malaki Starks was excellent in Week 1, tallying two solos, five assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Starks played 25 percent of his snaps in the box, something that will help boost his fantasy value if the trend continues. Tap Starks as a top-25 option for a plus Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.
Dane Belton is a DB3 play for Week 2 due to Minkah Fitzpatrick being sidelined with a groin injury. Plug him into lineups until the former All-Pro safety returns for the New York Jets.

Justin Reid played every snap in Week 1 and responded with five solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. His history suggests that he will settle in as a DB3/4, but he remains someone to monitor regardless of your roster needs. With that said, he does have a plus matchup on tap against the Baltimore Ravens, so feel free to fire him up as a DB3 option if you are cycling through waiver options post-draft.

Andrew Wingard showed out in Week 1, tallying three solos, one assist, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, one interception, and one pass defended. Wingard, having one of the standout IDP performances in Week 1, was on no one's bingo card, but that is not to say he hasn't shown flashes of his upside in previous seasons. For now, treat him as a DB3/4 or flex option for a plus Week 2 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. Start Wingard where possible.

Treydan Stukes was excellent in Week 1, piling up four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Stukes played every snap for the Raiders, relegating Isaiah Pola-Mao strictly to special teams duties. He did his job and then some in his NFL debut and looks like a potential IDP star in the making. Tap Stukes as a DB3 with DB2 upside for a plus Week 2 matchup against a Los Angeles Chargers team that had its struggles last week.
Andre Cisco made an IDP impact in Week 1, tallying six solos. Cisco played 88 percent of the snaps alongside Dane Belton, who filled in for the injured Minkah Fitzpatrick.

Byron Murphy was excellent in Week 1, notching seven solos, one assist, and one pass defended. Murphy is one of the better tackling corners in the game and offers CB1 upside even as a number one corner. Leave him on benches where possible for Week 2, with an eye on starting him during the byes.

Zyon McCollum showed out in Week 1, racking up eight solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended against the Cincinnati Bengals. McCollum has flashed before, most notably recording nine solos against the New York Jets. Zyon's performance puts him in the CB league mix as a CB2 option, but he has not yet shown enough to trust as a DB3 outside of the byes. That being said, McCollum averaged as many fantasy points per game as Tyler Nubin and Grant Delpit last season, so the potential is definitely there. Keep Zyon stashed where possible but keep him glued to benches for Week 2, despite the tasty matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Bryan Cook was excellent in Week 1, racking up four solos, two assists, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Cook makes for a solid DB3 option for Week 2, thanks to a plus matchup against the Houston Texans. Start him where needed.

Rookie safety Michael Taffee had himself a day in Week 1, racking up one solo, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended on 75 percent of the snaps. Taaffe surprised some by playing more snaps than supposed starter Dante Trader, who played just 47 percent of the snaps. Taaffe being locked into a starter's role puts him directly in the DB3 mix for the byes and the flex conversation otherwise. Start him as a DB4/flex option for what should be a busy afternoon at the office against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2.

Calen Bullock impressed in Week 1, racking up five solos, one assist, and one pass defended. Bullock is viewed more as bye week depth at the current time, but that could change if he can keep up the solo production despite playing deep for the bulk of his snaps. For now, leave him on benches for Week 2 despite the plus matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Rock Ya-Sin was excellent in Week 1, notching seven solos. Rock is a CB1 option for Week 2 and beyond, but is not someone to consider outside of the byes in 12 team leagues. Look elsewhere for Week 2.

James Pierre impressed in Week 1, registering four solos, one interception, and two passes defended. Pierre is a CB1 option who can fill in at DB during the byes. He is too boom-or-bust to trust over safeties most weeks, but has proven the ability to provide DB3 value in a pinch, especially in deeper leagues.

Quan Martin played just 38 percent of the snaps in Week 1, leaving him off the fantasy radar for the time being. Martin will be stuck behind Jeremy Reaves for the foreseeable future and is safe to drop outside of 32 team leagues.

Isaiah Pola-Mao looks like he is in a strict backup role for the Las Vegas Raiders. He lost the starting job to Treydan Stukes over the summer and played zero defensive snaps in Week 1. He is a drop in all formats, even dynasty leagues under 16 teams.
Malachi Moore played just 14 percent of the snaps in Week 1 and is off the fantasy radar until further notice.
